newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.5 pct in Nov -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.5 pct in Nov -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the first week of fiscal November versus October, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 6.3 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.3 percent in the week ended November 9, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Although results for the week varied among stores, the overall gain was in line with the pace of growth over the past two weeks, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
However, Eilenberg said the 0.5 percent increase was above retailers' expectations.

"Based on (retailers') expectations, we calculated that for the month there would be a decline in November compared to October," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "And it came in a little better than that."
Sales forecasts for November and December take into account calendar considerations that may skew results, said Eilenberg.
For instance, Eilenberg said some retailers were comparing against the week ended November 4 in 1995 and others were comparing against the week ended November 11.
"So their results for the whole month of November are going to be skewed," he said.
Apparel continued to be a strong seller at department stores, added Eilenberg.
